Lemma
[existence of harmonic coordinates]

Source: petersen:page-0422, petersen:page-0423 ↗ thm:pet-ch11-schauder-estimates ↗ rem:pet-ch11-divergence-form-laplace-beltrami 1. ch11:11.2.5Every point $p$ of an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold has a neighborhood $U$ with a harmonic coordinate system $x=(x^1,\dots ,x^n):U\to \mathbb {R}^n$, i.e. each $x^i$ is harmonic for $\Delta _g$.
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch11-harmonic-coordinates-exist \sketch Start with normal coordinates $y$ on a small Euclidean ball and solve $\Delta _gx^k=0$ with $x^k=y^k$ on the boundary by subsection 2.2. The divergence form in subsection 2.2 and the estimates of subsection 2.2 give

\[ \| x-y\| _{C^{2,\alpha }}\le C\| \Delta _gy\| _{C^\alpha }. \]

In normal coordinates $\Delta _gy(0)=0$, so the right side tends to zero with the radius. Thus $Dx$ remains invertible and $x$ is a harmonic coordinate system.

□
